publicationStmt.p: Amores Project working transcription, independently reviewed by a different agent on 10 September 2026. Not human-approved.

handDesc.handNote: Brown main writing and darker interventions are visible. Ink differences are recorded without assigning historical hands.

origin.p: The supplied library manifest dates the manuscript to the 10th/11th century; this does not date individual interventions.

surrogates.p: Library digital facsimile, PPN1844735508. The supplied manifest identifies the images as Public Domain Mark 1.0. Every verse in folios 68r, 68v was inspected for this first pass.

projectDesc.p: Source-grounded first pass of all 50 manuscript verses. No other witness or normalized edition was used as transcription input. Existing annotation coordinates provide navigation, not text. There are 50 original annotation rows for 50 distinct source verses, without duplicates. Every original rectangle was inspected and retained unchanged. Some rectangles include neighbouring text or exclude additions. sourceWitness=LL and panelId are provenance only; no other witness text was used.

correction.p: Uncertain letters are marked unclear and unreadable text gap. Darker ink is hi, not proof of erasure or a distinct hand. Actual additions use add; deletion or substitution is asserted only with visible evidence and qualified where needed. No unattested earlier reading is supplied.

normalization.p: Single source-oriented display. Ordinary allographs and long s are represented with standard Latin characters. Source spelling is preserved; word spacing and couplet layout are editorial. Explicit abbreviation expansions remain in TEI choices. Punctuation and unusual signs are schematic typographic equivalents, not exact pen-shape replicas.

punctuation.p: Visible significant punctuation and separation or insertion marks are retained. No modern sentence punctuation is supplied.

segmentation.p: Each l is one verse and one physical source line. Full-page inspection of folios68r and68v shows alternate physical lines inset; even-verse rend attributes record that observed layout. The lg groups are editorial elegiac couplets. Each verse has a stable ID and an existing facsimile rectangle. The rectangles may include neighbouring text and need not enclose marginal inscriptions.

interpretation.p: A different agent independently read all 50 source verses and investigated all 36 first-pass evidence notes. Source-supported decisions were reconciled directly; remaining uncertainty is documented without human-review assignments. The hash-bound review ledger records every note disposition. Independent agent review is not human scholarly approval.

revisionDesc.change: First source pass covering all 50 verses and visible interventions in folios 68r, 68v; awaiting a different agent's independent reading.

Independent source review of all 50 verses and 36 notes completed. Corrected the opening of verse 11 to Tu tua after reading the separate u following the initial T; encoded the visible expunction of e beneath added i in verse 22; represented the source et ligature in figuret at verse 24; retained visible terminal points in verses 16 and 26. Remaining marked or pale passages keep local uncertainty. Original zones and source-supported layout remain unchanged; zero human escalations.

div.head: Source evidence after independent review
div.note: An enlarged ornamental N opens the poem. The source adjective is formonsa, retained without normalization.
Final d of Sed is darker; no earlier letter is reconstructed.
Slender vertical marks cross the Nec/te and fieri/censura boundaries. They are retained schematically without declaring text cancelled. The et ending of iubet is a ligature.
Rogo is dark and remains readable; no prior state is inferred.
The ss of peccasse and final e of negare are dark. Word separation in quae cumque is editorial.
The a of famosam is dark and crossed by an oblique stroke. Its readable current form is retained without reconstructing an erased predecessor.

The ending or of furor and following barred e are dark. The latter is explicitly expanded est. A tall zigzag-like sign stands to the right; it is retained schematically with unspecified function. Additional far-margin strokes are documented.
A slender vertical stroke follows facias. A further tall sign at the right follows the preceding verse decoration; its exact punctuation function is uncertain.

Populum and summouet have explicit nasal suspension bars, both expanded in choices. The et ending of summouet is a ligature; the initial s of sera is dark. Paired right-margin strokes have unspecified function.

Independent enlargement shows a separate u immediately after the tall opening T, giving Tu tua. The first pass omitted this u and read the initial as I. A slender terminal stroke has unspecified function.

The baseline reads Commisi. A small dark raised mark near its final letters is not securely separable as a letter and is documented without a reconstructed addition. A vertical stroke crosses the middle of indiciumque.
The source baseline reads saltem ue. Abbreviated q with a que sign is added above the ue area, explicitly expanded que. No baseline deletion is asserted. A slender stroke follows melior.
Nequitiam is contracted with a nasal bar over final a. Lo of locus is dark. The visible source opening is Est qui.
The final is-region of Deliciis and sit are darker. A small point follows imple. A right-margin x is documented without assigning a correction function.
A slender stroke follows exieris. It is retained schematically without cancelling the word.
A slender stroke follows Absit. The following conjunction is an et ligature.
The source writes podori. Its vowel is retained without normalizing it to pudori.

The source has baseline femore, with a point immediately below the final e and i above it. Independent enlargement supports expunction of e and replacement by the above-line i; both states are preserved.

A dark spot follows the final m of uenerem; it does not clearly establish cancellation. Independent enlargement confirms that figuret ends with the same et ligature used elsewhere, now represented explicitly.
The e of uoces is dark. The current word remains readable.
The source adjective is metuentem. No alternate wording is imported.
The fitea-region of diffiteatur has darker letters. No earlier word is reconstructed.
The final ti of mitti and p of recipique are dark. A short horizontal mark crosses the re/ci region of recipique. The current reading is retained without inferring deletion.
The ss-region of pressus is pale and overlapped and remains unclear. An r is added above after p in pior. A vertical stroke follows est; the components are retained separately.
The o of turbatos is dark; no erased earlier ending is inferred.
The r of parcere is dark and followed by a slender boundary stroke before parce. Source fame is retained without adding a separate a.

The first et ligature closes hebet; abit is written above it. A slender diagonal mark also crosses that area. Because cancellation of the whole ligature is not secure, the baseline and addition remain separate. The following conjunction is another et ligature.
The source phrase is sed tecum, retained with editorial word separation.

The pale group after equidem appears irquitam but remains unclear; a short horizontal stroke crosses its middle and another separates it from ne. C is added above ne before que celare. No familiar reading is restored and no unobserved letters are supplied.

The pale baseline noun after falsi appears muneris and remains unclear. Criminis is written above it; small horizontal marks below do not securely establish the extent of cancellation. Both are preserved without a conjectural erased state.
Several pale and dark strokes occur across in media deprensa. The current letters remain readable, but the marks do not establish a recoverable earlier phrase or a distinct hand.
R is added above between b and a of proba, preserving the baseline and insertion separately.
A slender vertical stroke follows fuerint. It is an unspecified mark, not a supplied letter.
The initial l of lumina is dark. The current word is retained.
A slender terminal stroke follows duobus. No textual function is assigned.
A vertical stroke follows causa. A terminal colon-like sign and long stroke precede the enlarged Q opening3.15; the next source line is not a heading.
